cohort: The study included 168 patients with uterine fibroids who underwent either open or laparoscopic myomectomy between October 2017 and July 2023, with diverse motivations for uterus-preservation, including a desire for future pregnancies in 51.2% of cases.
finding: Both open and laparoscopic myomectomy surgeries showed high patient satisfaction, symptom alleviation, and comparable pregnancy results, but laparoscopy demonstrated a preference in terms of lower recurrence risk and fewer cesarean section recommendations.
mod_finding: Cesarean section recommendations were significantly more frequent in the post-laparotomy group (86.6%) compared to the laparoscopy group (36.6%).
